event_title: Other fall to lower level 11 to 15 feet
evidence: NAICS 561311 employer doing construction work: "scaffold"; "fall to lower level"
narrative: A temporary employee's nail bag caught on the brick layer scaffold he was working from causing him to lose balance and fall approximately twelve feet to the ground below fracturing his hip. The employee was admitted to the hospital for surgery.

event_title: Other fall to lower level less than 6 feet
evidence: NAICS 561320 employer doing construction work: "under construction"; "fall to lower level"
narrative: On October 22, 2015, at approximately 2:00 pm, an employee was sweeping the floor of a loading dock located on a building under construction, opened an overhead door, and fell approximately 4 feet to the ground below. The employee was admitted to the hospital for a broken hip.

event_title: Fall through surface or existing opening 11 to 15 feet
evidence: NAICS 561320 employer doing construction work: "construction site"; "fell 15 feet"
narrative: An employee was attempting to remove a roof panel at a construction site when he lost his footing and fell 15 feet through an opening in the roof. He broke both wrists and was hospitalized. Fall protection was worn at the time of the incident.

event_title: Other fall to lower level 26 to 30 feet
evidence: NAICS 561320 employer doing construction work: "roofing"; "fell off"
narrative: An employee was working on a flat roof rolling out the rubber roofing and fell off the edge of the roof to the ground approximately 24-26 feet below. The employee suffered a fractured skull, shoulder and wrist.

event_title: Other fall to lower level less than 6 feet
evidence: NAICS 561311 employer doing construction work: "hanging sheet rock"; "fall to lower level"
narrative: An employee was hanging sheet rock from a six foot A-frame ladder. The employee fell and fractured his right wrist.

event_title: Other fall to lower level 16 to 20 feet
evidence: NAICS 561320 employer doing construction work: "scaffold"; "fall to lower level"
narrative: An employee was removing the crane hoisting straps from an installed wooden beam when he fell approximately 20 ft. from a mobile scaffold to the ground. The employee sustained trauma to the face and right leg.

event_title: Other fall to lower level 11 to 15 feet
evidence: NAICS 561311 employer doing construction work: "concrete forms"; "fall to lower level"
narrative: An employee was working on concrete forms approximately 12 to 13 feet from a lower level when she fell to the ground, breaking both ankles.

employer: Pacesetter Personnel Service of Florida, Inc.
event_title: Fall from collapsing structure or equipment, unspecified
evidence: NAICS 561320 employer doing construction work: "excavat"; "Fall from"
narrative: The injured employee and another employee were removing a water pump and moving hoses when the ground they were standing on gave way. The injured employee fell forward into the excavation and directly onto the form beam sustaining injuries to the left side of their chest including broken ribs.

event_title: Other fall to lower level less than 6 feet
evidence: NAICS 561320 employer doing construction work: "trench"; "fall to lower level"
narrative: A temporary employee was entering a trench that was 4 feet by 8 feet and 4 feet deep to help install a propane gas tank. While entering the trench, which had wood and aluminum siding installed, the employee slipped and fell. The siding then lacerated his left forearm, requiring hospitalization and surgery.

event_title: Other fall to lower level, unspecified
evidence: NAICS 561320 employer doing construction work: "drip edge"; "fall to lower level"
narrative: An employee was installing a drip edge along the roof eave and fell striking an air conditioner during the fall to the ground. The employee was hospitalized for back fractures.

event_title: Fall to lower level, unspecified
evidence: NAICS 561320 employer doing construction work: "under construction"; "fell from"
narrative: A temporary employee was laying down insulation in the attic of a commercial building under construction. The employee fell from the attic to the concrete floor and suffered a concussion.

event_title: Fall from collapsing structure or equipment less than 6 feet
evidence: NAICS 561311 employer doing construction work: "scaffold"; "Fall from"
narrative: On 5/06/2019, at 9:00 a.m., a temporary employee was installing ceiling tiles from a scaffold. She went to move the 3-foot scaffold, but the scaffold broke and she fell onto the concrete ground fracturing her right wrist which required surgery.

event_title: Other fall to lower level, unspecified
evidence: NAICS 561320 employer doing construction work: "installing insulation"; "fell off"
narrative: A temporary employee was on a 10-foot ladder, installing insulation and doing mastic duct work. The employee came into contact with an exposed temporary wire, was shocked, and fell off the third or fourth rung of the ladder. Along with the electric shock, he suffered a broken left heel.

event_title: Other fall to lower level 11 to 15 feet
evidence: NAICS 561311 employer doing construction work: "demolition"; "fall to lower level"
narrative: A temporary employee fell through a manhole at a demolition site, landing 14 feet below and suffering a severe head injury and broken ribs.

event_title: Other fall to lower level 6 to 10 feet
evidence: NAICS 561311 employer doing construction work: "scaffold"; "fall to lower level"
narrative: A temporary employee was on the second rung of a ladder installing a window on the third floor of a residence. The suction cups on the window failed causing him to fall approximately 10 feet. He fell through the scaffolding on the second floor and then rolled down the stairwell to the first floor. The employee sustained fractured discs and a fractured hip.

event_title: Other fall to lower level less than 6 feet
evidence: NAICS 561320 employer doing construction work: "scaffold"; "fall to lower level"
narrative: A temporary employee was trying to get off a scaffold when he slipped and fell, landing on a piece of angle iron about 3 feet below. The employee suffered a broken hip and was hospitalized.

event_title: Other fall to lower level 6 to 10 feet
evidence: NAICS 561320 employer doing construction work: "trench"; "fall to lower level"
narrative: A temporary employee was bracing a foundation wall with a 2x4 board. He was attempting to get it to a 45 degree angle and was leaning on the board to secure it in place. The board snapped and the employee fell head-first into the 9-foot-deep trench. The employee sustained a broken tibia and fibula as well as heel fracture.

event_title: Other fall to lower level  unspecified
evidence: NAICS 561320 employer doing construction work: "scaffold"; "fell off"
narrative: A temporary employee was standing on scaffolding removing oxidation with a torch when they fell off and landed on an anvil on the ground, resulting in fractures to their L1 -L5 vertebrae and a left kidney laceration.

event_title: Fall to lower level from collapsing structure or equipment  6 to 30 feet
evidence: NAICS 561320 employer doing construction work: "scaffold"; "Fall to lower level from"
narrative: On December 22, 2024, two temporary employees were working from a combination steel scaffolding with wood planks when the scaffold collapsed. The employees fell 14-15 feet to the lower level. One employee was treated at the hospital for back pain and released. The other employee was hospitalized with six stitches over his right eye, multiple contusions, and liver lacerations.

event_title: Other fall to lower level  unspecified
evidence: NAICS 561311 employer doing construction work: "scaffold"; "fall to lower level"
narrative: An employee was cutting wood and installing wood backing in an elevator shaft. He retrieved a rolling baker scaffold from the drywall crew and positioned it near the work area. He placed the wood on the scaffold and climbed up. While nailing a piece into place, he lost his balance and slipped. To steady himself, he grabbed the newly installed wood, but the wood detached and he fell into the elevator shaft. He sustained fractures to his ribs and pelvis and a laceration to the head.
